one_liner: Invoicing, payment collection (payment links via UPI/card/bank transfer) and NBFC-funded invoice financing for Indian SMEs.
sub_sector: SME payments and invoice financing (lending service provider to NBFC partners)
ask: INR 30 Cr at INR 180 Cr post-money; seeking a lead
business_model: 0.4% fee on payments collected plus about 1.2% a month on invoices financed, with financing funded through NBFC partners. Founder-stated October 2026: INR 86 Cr payment volume, INR 78 L net revenue, 1,150 SMEs, 58% gross margin.

founders.background_claimed: 10 years in transaction banking; led SME product at a private bank.
founders.background_verified: Not verified. LinkedIn link is a placeholder; the bank is not named. Searches for name + Settlr + Mumbai returned only unrelated invoice-financing companies.

founders.name: Sonal Iyer
founders.background_claimed: 8 years in payments engineering at a large fintech.
founders.background_verified: Not verified. LinkedIn link is a placeholder; the fintech is not named. Search for name + Settlr + CTO + Mumbai returned nothing matching.

claims.text: Rahul Mehta (CEO) has 10 years in transaction banking and led SME product at a private bank.
claims.note: Deck and form agree; employer not named.

claims.text: Sonal Iyer (CTO) has 8 years in payments engineering at a large fintech.
claims.note: Deck and form agree; employer not named.

claims.text: No public footprint found for either founder; both LinkedIn links are placeholders.
October 2026 payment volume INR 86 Cr and net revenue INR 78 L, from 1,150 SME customers.
claims.note: Deck and form agree. Cross-check: 1,150 SMEs x INR 6,800 average monthly fees = INR 78.2 L, consistent.

claims.text: The month-by-month volume trend (Jun 52 to Oct 86 Cr) is an assumed ordering; the PDF extraction listed 79, 86, 70, 52, 61.
claims.note: Only October (INR 86 Cr) is confirmed by the form.

claims.text: Revenue comes from a 0.4% fee on payments collected and about 1.2% a month on invoices financed, funded through NBFC partners.
claims.note: Our arithmetic: 0.4% x INR 86 Cr = ~INR 34 L, so ~INR 44 L/month would come from financing. If Settlr keeps the full 1.2%/month that implies ~INR 36 Cr financed in the month while the NBFC funds it, which only works if Settlr shares credit risk or reports gross charges. Split not disclosed.

claims.text: 45% of the INR 30 Cr Series A is earmarked for a 'financing book'.
claims.note: Settlr says financing is funded by NBFC partners and does not claim its own NBFC licence. Equity going into a book implies either balance-sheet lending (needs RBI registration) or a default loss guarantee/co-lending arrangement; which one is not stated.

claims.text: Under RBI's digital lending framework, default loss guarantee (DLG/FLDG) cover from a lending service provider is capped at 5% of the loan portfolio.
claims.note: June 2023 DLG guidelines, consolidated into the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 (8 May 2025). If Settlr guarantees its NBFC partners' losses, any first-loss cover above 5% would be non-compliant; credit risk above that sits with the NBFC.

claims.text: RBI rules require loan servicing and repayment to go directly to the regulated lender's bank account without any pass-through or pool account of a third party.
claims.note: Relevant because Settlr also collects buyer payments on its payment links; repayments of financed invoices cannot route through a Settlr-controlled pool account.

claims.text: Unit economics: CAC INR 14,500 per SME, 7-month payback, 58% gross margin, 112% net revenue retention.
claims.note: Our arithmetic: INR 6,800 x 58% = ~INR 3,940 gross profit per SME per month, implying ~3.7-month payback, not 7. The stated 7 months may include other costs; method not given.

claims.text: Deck market sizing understates its own inputs by 10x: SOM is shown as INR 6,750 Cr from 15,000 SMEs x INR 4.5 Cr, which equals INR 67,500 Cr; SAM (400K x 4.5 Cr) and TAM (2.1M x 4.5 Cr) are likewise 10x below their stated products.
claims.note: Also: current average volume per SME is ~INR 0.9 Cr a year (INR 86 Cr x 12 / 1,150), far below the INR 4.5 Cr per SME assumed. Sizing should be rebuilt from revenue, not volume.

claims.text: Settlr prices financing at about 1.2% a month, positioned against informal invoice discounting at 24 to 36% a year.
claims.note: 1.2%/month is ~14.4% a year simple. Deck promises early payment 'against any invoice', which implies taking on unrated buyer risk.

claims.text: Credlix advertises invoice-discounting financing for MSMEs from 1% per month.
claims.note: Pricing benchmark: Settlr's 1.2% is not cheaper than funded competitors.

claims.text: TReDS is an RBI-authorised electronic platform for discounting MSME bills on large corporates; RXIL, M1xchange and Invoicemart operate platforms.
claims.note: Regulated, auction-priced alternative for SME invoices on large buyers; Settlr does not mention TReDS.

claims.text: Mumbai-headquartered Cashinvoice raised USD 3.4 M (INR 28.2 Cr) Series A in Feb 2024 for invoice-discounting / supply-chain finance for MSMEs.
Seed round of INR 9 Cr raised in 2024, led by two institutional funds; cap table founders 58%, seed investors 30%, ESOP 12%.
claims.note: No press or database record of a Settlr seed round found. Implied seed post-money ~INR 30 Cr; ask is INR 180 Cr post (~6x).

claims.text: Name collision: 'Settlrs' is an unrelated Bengaluru office-equipment rental company (founded 2017), not Settlr Fintech.
claims.note: Search results also surfaced an unrelated co-living startup 'Settl' (not opened, not cited). Any database lookup on the name must be checked against the CIN.

claims.text: Team of 31; both founders full-time since 2023; incorporated April 2023.
claims.note: Deck and form agree on team size.

claims.text: Acquisition mix: CA and accountant partners 40%, direct sales 35%, inbound and referrals 25%.
18-month plan: INR 300 Cr monthly volume, 4,500 SMEs and break-even operations.
Founder-listed key risks: credit losses on financed invoices, dependence on NBFC partners, regulation of digital lending.
Raising INR 30 Cr Series A at INR 180 Cr post-money, looking for a lead; four Series A funds in conversation.

research_notes: Deck and form agree on every number; the one deck-internal issue is market sizing that is 10x below its own inputs, plus an assumed chart ordering. The decisive open question is credit-risk allocation with NBFC partners (DLG 5% cap; 45% of raise to a 'financing book'). Web quotes were extracted via a fetch tool and should be re-verified with verify_web.
